summary: The mechanism (fold the hi accumulator into the lo GEMM's beta=1 epilogue so the 0.9-1.1 us add node and its graph gap disappear) is real and the per-shape router rows can read it, but the change paragraph's out-of-place form 'acc = torch.addmm(acc, x, router_lo_t, ...)' makes PyTorch copy acc into a fresh result with its own elementwise kernel before the GEMM, so as written it swaps add for copy and will most likely read flat for a reason unrelated to the mechanism. One control with out=acc (in-place, no copy) makes a flat primary interpretable.
justification: On master (router-hilo-at-m8, job aa3d033c208e4511) every router row with m>1 is nvjet splitK x2 (7.9-10.5 us), splitKreduce x2 (3.3-3.8 us), vectorized_elementwise add 0.9-1.1 us; 14.15/14.51/15.03/16.21/17.66 us at m=8/16/32/128/256 against floors 1.8-2.7 us, ~0.4 us gap per node. Removing one node saves ~1.3-1.5 us, 8-10% of a router row, readable per shape (untouched rows scatter ~+/-3%); ~1.5% geomean, at the CI edge, so classify from router rows. verify_1 (m=8) is now on hi/lo and must be expected faster, not flat; decode_1 (m=1) is the only flat control. Weakest link: out-of-place addmm with a 2-D self and beta != 0 runs at::native::copy_(result, self) as its own vectorized_elementwise kernel, same node count as mm + add, and the profile would look identical to master. Second: addmm.dtype/dtype_out overloads must exist in the image's torch. Third: cuBLAS may pick a different algorithm for beta=1. Numerics: summation order only, ~1e-7 relative.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: created the torch.mm hi/lo path this change edits; substrate, not a confounder.
router-hilo-at-m8 (ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS 8 -> 1): widens reach to the m=8 row; the expected 'verify_1 flat' entry is stale and must be faster. Not a causal confounder.
Attribution base: compare per-shape medians against router-hilo-at-m8's job aa3d033c208e4511, not the stale BEST.json starter.
interference: ab-revert/ab-tune of landed items is pointless. What is needed is a control on the hypothesis's own sub-change: the primary is both 'beta=1 epilogue' and 'out-of-place addmm', and the latter re-introduces a copy_ launch. A flat primary would be ambiguous between 'beta epilogue not free' and 'addmm copied self'. A control with out=acc resolves it. If the dispatcher may amend the primary to out=acc, drop the companion. No second companion.
rules_flags: None blocking: fp32 accumulation and hi/lo split kept; acc allocated inside the timed call; no host syncs; branching on shapes only.
An overload probe in prepare() must run on synthetic tensors, set a plain module-level bool, and print the chosen path.
out=acc in place is fine under graph capture; acc is fresh every call.

companions.change: From the parent's branch (master with sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity and router-hilo-at-m8; ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS = 1), apply the parent's change with one difference: the lo GEMM accumulates in place into the hi result instead of allocating a new output. In kernel_fn's router branch above ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS replace 'acc = torch.mm(x, state["router_hi_t"], out_dtype=torch.float32); acc += torch.mm(x, state["router_lo_t"], out_dtype=torch.float32)' with 'acc = torch.mm(x, state["router_hi_t"], out_dtype=torch.float32); torch.addmm(acc, x, state["router_lo_t"], beta=1.0, alpha=1.0, out_dtype=torch.float32, out=acc); return acc'. Because out is the same tensor as self, at::native::copy_(result, self) early-returns and no elementwise kernel is launched; cuBLAS applies beta=1 in its splitKreduce and writes D over C. In prepare(), after building the hi/lo tensors, probe once on synthetic CUDA tensors (a = torch.zeros(2, 256, fp32); torch.addmm(a, torch.zeros(2, 8192, bf16), state["router_lo_t"], beta=1.0, alpha=1.0, out_dtype=torch.float32, out=a)) inside try/except, set a module-level bool _ADDMM_INPLACE_OK, and print it; kernel_fn uses the in-place addmm when the flag is True and the parent's two-statement mm + add when False, so a missing overload never fails the run and the log_tail states which path was timed. Everything else stays: prepare()'s hi/lo split, the fp32 F.linear path at m<=1, the bf16 layers on _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl. Expected kernel sequence per router row with m>1: nvjet splitK, splitKreduce, nvjet splitK, splitKreduce, and no vectorized_elementwise node at all.

expected.why: m=8 is on hi/lo on master (14.15 us); the add node and its ~0.4 us gap go away, ~1.3 us or ~9%
same, 14.51 us with a 0.9 us add node
same, 15.03 us with a 1.0 us add node
same at m=128, 16.21 us with a 1.1 us add node
same at m=256, 17.66 us with a 1.1 us add node
m=1 stays on F.linear fp32; control

companions.reason: Separates 'cuBLAS's beta=1 epilogue is not cheaper than the separate add' from 'PyTorch's out-of-place addmm re-introduced an elementwise copy kernel'; this is the form to promote if it gains.
